did.unittitle: Andrea Lurie Papers
did.abstract: This collection contains materials related to the women's movement and lesbian rights in New York State, especially the Capital Region in the 1970s, as well as materials related to Lurie's professional efforts as an archeologist.
did.physloc: The materials are located onsite in the department.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Processed in 2006 January by Amy C. Schindler.
Reprocessed in 2025 April by Meghan Slaff.

bioghist.head: Biographical History
bioghist.p: Andrea Lurie was an active member of the womens movement in the New York Capital Region during the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s. This included founding and working with such organizations as Capital District Women (CDW), Women's Counseling Collective, and Tri-City Women's Center. She was involved in the planning of the Womens "Revolution", a utopian society that would promote equality, same-sex relationships, and polyamory while discouraging traditional family dynamics. Lurie was also responsible for executing the Women's Day March in Albany, N.Y.

Professionally, Andrea Lurie was an archeologist. She used her education to promote feminism and better understand the social dynamics responsible for misogyny. A majority of the published materials within the collection relate to her research.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection includes materials related to the women's movement and lesbian rights with an emphasis on the Capital Region of New York. Andrea Lurie collected photographs from Women's Day in Albany, posters, material related to projects in Albany, correspondence, drafts of manuscripts, and Lurie's own speeches. Records of particular interest are those of the group Capital District Women and the Women's Counseling Collective. Also included are pamphlets, newsletters, journals, and periodicals.

Having worked as an archeologist in her professional career, there are also materials related to archeology including academic journals, conference materials, and archeological societies. Though many of the materials only tangentially relate to the feminist movement, they help to show the extent of Lurie's personal and professional endeavors.

arrangement.head: Arrangement of the Collection
arrangement.p: The collection has no series and is arranged alphabetically.

separatedmaterial.head: Separated Materials
separatedmaterial.p: The archivist transferred six volumes of "Signs: Journal of Women in Culture and Society" to the book division of the Special Collections, including: Volume 1 Nos. 1, 2, 3 (parts 1 and 2), 4; Volume 2 Nos. 1, 2, 3; Volume 3 Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4; Volume 4 Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4; Volume 5 Nos. 1, 2, 3; and Volume 6 Nos. 1 and 2. They will be catalogued and included in the University Library Catalog.

acqinfo.head: Acquisition Information
acqinfo.p: All items in this manuscript group were donated to the University Libraries, M.E. Grenander Department of Special Collections & Archives by Andrea Lurie in1994 June.
